title: Pixel-first physician product shell: composer with answer modes, one mascot, profile, materials and a separate de-identification tool

problem.user_segment: physicians across the six launch specialties
problem.job: ask one question, choose how deep the answer goes, launch a job, keep a personal library and de-identify a document — on one coherent shell
problem.observed_failure: The input reads as a plain textarea with example chips inside it; there is no answer mode in the model; quick agents and suggestions share one rail without hierarchy; nine mascots are line-art variants; the profile is a chip list without identity, source priorities or a default answer depth; de-identification exists as a library and server-side redaction but has no physician-facing tool; card media is stretched by the tablet column.
evidence: components/portal/portal-input.tsx: textarea in a grey box, examples rendered inside the form
lib/agents/types.ts: no answer mode on AgentRun.input or UserProfile
components/portal/mascot.tsx: stroked line-art body with per-variant palettes
lib/clinical-case/anonymizer.ts used only by server-side risk.ts and the legacy case surface
app/styles/product-surface.css: .pt-card.has-media media column with min-height 100% and object-fit cover

hypothesis: If the shell follows the agreed references pixel-first — one composer surface, three answer modes carried into run metadata, a suggestion row, three quick jobs, one mascot, a profile that the personalization layer reads, a materials library and a separate de-identification tool, with deterministic media geometry — physicians recognise one product and return to it.
kill_criteria: a suggestion or a quick agent changes the answer mode
a request is stored without its answer mode
the materials route renders the de-identification workflow or the reverse
a mascot is rendered as a different character or exposed to assistive technology
a source image or a rejected media attempt is rendered on a card
a control is cut off or overlaps text at 390, 768 or 1440
the mode control is simulated visually without reaching execution
